name: Taillard Scheduling Instances
description: The Taillard instances are a standard set of benchmark problems for basic scheduling, introduced by Eric Taillard to give metaheuristics a common, hard testbed. The best-known set covers the permutation flow-shop problem with 120 instances across twelve size classes (from 20 jobs x 5 machines up to 500 jobs x 20 machines), with companion sets for the job-shop and open-shop problems. Schedules are scored by makespan (Cmax) relative to published best-known or lower-bound values.
evaluation_method: makespan gap to best-known / lower bound
typical_sota_score: Smaller flow-shop instances are closed to optimality; the largest classes remain open and are actively improved by metaheuristics and matheuristics.
reputation: A metaheuristics standard for flow-shop and job-shop scheduling; one of the most frequently cited scheduling benchmark sets.
notes: Not an LLM benchmark; targets scheduling metaheuristics and exact methods. Several large instances still have a gap between best-known makespan and proven lower bounds. Complements the OR-Library scheduling sets (Fisher-Thompson, Lawrence).

institutions: HEIG-VD / University of Applied Sciences Western Switzerland
